dedupe_keys.name: hospital efficiency project hep discrete event simulation for orthopaedic elective theatre and ward planning

description: This simulation helps a hospital plan its planned (elective) orthopaedic surgery by testing how the operating theatre timetable, the number of ward beds and delayed discharges interact. The producers are Alison Harper, Thomas Monks and Martin Pitt of the University of Exeter, who built it in the Hospital Efficiency Project and report it using the STRESS guidelines for discrete-event simulation. The model represents patients for five types of elective orthopaedic surgery moving from theatre to ward, with lengths of stay and a share of patients whose discharge is delayed, and users can change the theatre schedule, bed numbers, lengths of stay and delay settings. Coverage is one orthopaedic service with parameters the user can change. The Python code is available free on GitHub and Zenodo under the MIT licence, with an online web app, a Binder notebook environment and a separate Docker deployment package. Caveats: built for one specialty, default parameters should be replaced with local data, and the Python environment is pinned to an older version (3.8). Simulation uses: sizing beds and theatre sessions for elective recovery, and showing how delayed discharges caused by shortages in community care block surgical capacity. Related records: the IPACS model (model-ipacs-discharge-to-assess-capacity) models the discharge pathways that cause those delays, and the SimPy healthcare models (model-simpy-streamlit-healthcare-des) come from the same group.
